And there came a time when those troops withdrew, but before that occurred there were a series of events that occurred that I'd like to go through with you, just to make sure that we have them chronologically accurate, which is that, I believe, you told us that on May 4th there was a decision by the leadership in Belgrade to remove the troops within 15 days.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And that was at a point in time when there was a decision made that there would be no, and I've forgotten the exact language, but there would be no involvement or interest in these other areas by FRY.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now whether that was on May 4th -- May 4th or later, but in May. I believe that was the 197th session of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that's correct. Now, with regard to date-wise, what would occur, what that would mean that if all things went smoothly, the JNA would have been out of there by the 19th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fifteen days later.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Between those two dates, however, the Security Council passed a resolution. That was --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- on the 15th; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on the 15th of May, the Security Council -- that was 752, was it not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on that -- the Security Council, on the 15th of May, indicated that as far as they were concerned, those troops should depart within nine days.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be the term of the resolution, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Nine days from which date?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: From the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So they were given an extension.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would seem that they were either -- either they were both operating on the same line without knowing or they were given an extension, and let's assume -- I assume they were given an extension but I don't know that to be the case directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But if we were to follow the Security Council's resolution with regard to when the troops should have left, that would have taken us to May 24th; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, the next time there was a pronouncement by the Security Council, that was on the 30th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was 752, the passage of 752?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think the previous one was 752.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I do apologise. It was 757?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So now essentially what happens is that if all things were working perfectly, we're late in terms of getting those troops out of there.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're six days late.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, what was the date that the troops actually left?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. A lot of them never left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Would the date of June 9th be of help to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would not. Okay. Are you aware of the evacuation -- we've had evidence here and heard evidence here of the evacuation by the JNA from barracks in Sarajevo around the 8th and 9th of June. Does that assist you at all in terms of a time when the JNA was pulling out of the area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I can't recall those particular events. I know there was an attempted evacuation in early May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been an attempted withdrawal from barracks in Sarajevo in early May, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, between the time that the first indication was made to withdraw the troops in early May up to the 30th, as you sit here today, can you tell us whether or not there were any attacks on the JNA forces that were in, for example, Sarajevo by any of the other parties?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned the attack early in -- early in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details of any military activity after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to the international -- the international response, are you aware of the report of the Secretary-General of the 30th of May, 1992, in which he discusses the issue of the withdrawal of the units of the JNA? Is that a document that you're familiar with, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may -- I can't place it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have 1D00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, what would you like to do with 65 ter 6830?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would like to have that admitted as a Defence exhibit or -- yes, as a Defence exhibit, if I could, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will be Exhibit D5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I thank you, Your Honour, for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are most welcome. Now, what do you want on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one, madam, 6830 or 1D00-1449.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 6830, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, you indicated in your report when you were discussing the documents that you relied upon that you relied upon records of international organisations, primarily UN, and my first question: Is this one of the documents that you relied upon with regard to, or that you reviewed with regard to the drafting of this particular report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the heading at the top of the page? I don't recognise the number. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you -- if we could have -- if we could go through this document together. This document discusses the background of the situation concerning the withdrawal of the JNA. In paragraph 2 it discusses a letter that the secretary general received on the 17th of May, from the Chief of General Staff of the JNA requesting assistance and the safe withdrawal of JNA troops from Bosnia-Herzegovina and particularly from Sarajevo, Pozaric, and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Can Defence provide a Rule 65 ter number or a copy of that document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But is that a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your colleague is asking for a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Has it been released?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's not a 65 ter document. It's a Defence document, and it has been released.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is meant by "released"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That means it goes -- the way that I understand e-court to work - and I'm a dinosaur, so I could be saying this wrong - but they have documents on a list which they upload into the system and then they release those documents so they're available so they can come to all of us. When we have documents that are not on their 65 ter list that we would like to use, then we upload them into the system. That's what Daniela does. She uploads them into the system, and then she releases them so they're available for all the parties to have the benefit of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a concept completely distinct from disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. It's the way you work -- it's the way I understand you work with e-court. I'm pretty much a paper man myself, Your Honour, but that's what I understand is happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just while we're on this, the Defence is supposed to provide the Prosecution with a list of exhibits that they're going to use at the end of the examination-in-chief, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those documents were released, my understanding was, before the examination-in-chief was finished today. I mean, that was my direction, and my understanding was those documents were released.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. We were not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that what you understand? I didn't understand the question by the Prosecutor to refer to "release" here. I thought it referred to disclosure when she said, "Your Honour, the Defence is supposed to provide the Prosecution with a list of exhibits." I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think I might know -- I think I might know -- what occurred, is the documents were released, but you might not have gotten a notification of it, is I think what happened. And I do apologise for that, and I will take care of that on my side. This is our very first, you know, release of documents. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is the fifth exhibit of the Defence. You have released four before, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a first Defence exhibit. I thought that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The fifth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thought you did have it. I knew it had been released to you, and I thought you were aware of it, and I'll have the mechanism taken care of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You accept that, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We weren't advised that the documents had been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Moving on to paragraph 4, the Secretary-General through UNPROFOR has obtained certain information about the status of the units, although he indicates not completely authenticated. I'm going to go down to paragraph 6(a), which is discussing the issue of the evacuation of soldiers who were in the Marsal Tito barracks in Sarajevo, and it states: "Some 600 to 1,000 soldiers are blocked in the Marsal Tito barracks at Sarajevo, with nearly 200 vehicles. Negotiations on the evacuation of these barracks continued until 27 May 1992, when they broke down following a mortar attack which killed some 16 civilians in central Sarajevo. On 30 May 1992, the barracks came under attack from rocket-propelled grenades and flame-throwers fired by the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina." There's further information concerning what's occurring in another barracks, and those are the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks, when, while the JNA forces were in the process of withdrawing during the night, a convoy which was accompanied by UNPROFOR, they were attacked by Serb irregulars opposed to the terms of their withdrawal and by units of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia, and they lost their way. Turning to -- skipping paragraph sub (c) and going to paragraph 7, the Secretary-General opines that: "It will be apparent from the foregoing that the issue of the deblocking and safe withdrawal of the remaining JNA troops from their barracks at Bosnia and Herzegovina has become linked to other problems which have caused continuing conflict in that Republic ..." and then he goes on to discuss another matter of some concern. We learn from here that UNPROFOR has received indications that the JNA is willing to leave the bulk of its weapons behind upon withdrawal, but there is an argument about that. With regard to paragraph 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Guy-Smith, I don't want to interfere with your cross-examination, but you're reading quite a number of paragraphs to the witness without soliciting any response from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Let me stop. Point taken, Your Honour. Let me stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The information that's contained -- that we have discussed thus far or that I have pointed out thus far, is that information which you deemed to be relevant with regard to an understanding of the historical context in which the Bosnian Serb leadership was operating, as it relates to the report you have submitted to us and the testimony that you have given to us?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think some of the things that are mentioned in this report could be useful in considering that context. I'm not sure how accurate some of this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, independent --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note on the previous page, paragraph 6, there was some information that is related to something that is in the report, but I don't think it adds much, and I wasn't particularly occupied with the issue of detailing events at this particular time. But I note that it does say that: "Those who were not citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina are said by Belgrade authorities, barely 20 per cent of the total. Most of these are believed to have withdrawn already in Serbia and Montenegro. Some of them have been subjected to attack during their withdrawal. Others, however, remained in various garrisons in Bosnia-Herzegovina, especially in Serbian-controlled areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take it for purposes of our discussion that you find that particular piece of information to be relevant because it's information that you find was found in your report in another fashion; correct? But the balance of information that I discussed with you is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that information was in the report. I think what's in the report is the discussion in the Presidency in early May. I think in my testimony we used a document, a speech by General Gvero, I believe it was, at which he dealt with this particular issue. As I said, I did not look at this document at that time. If I had, I -- or the other document. If I had, I might have included them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, turning our attention to paragraph 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you -- okay, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Turning our attention to paragraph 8, it indicates that there's uncertainty about who exercises political control over the Serb forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina has further complicated the situation. Going down a bit, it says: "A senior JNA representative from Belgrade, General Nedjeljko Boskovic ..." is he an individual you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. "Has conducted discussions with the Bosnian-Herzegovina Presidency." Now, the Presidency at that time would be, as you've indicated to us, would be the three people; correct? That would have been --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is, I believe, a reference to the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see, okay.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "But it has become clear that his word is not binding on the commander of the army of the Serbian republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, General Mladic."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Going to paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are mindful of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, my. My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Unless you want to wind up the point. It's just that I heard you now going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I could finish the document -- you know what, it's going to take a few more minutes. Rather than put pressure on any of the people who are working in many senses probably much harder than I in terms of making this work, this would be an appropriate time. I do apologise for taking longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, one matter, a point of clarification on transcript page 92, the document -- Rule 65 ter number 06830 was admitted and given Defence Exhibit number 5. What are Defence Exhibits number 1 to 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They were given on previous days, ma'am, I wouldn't remember them at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour. No, I withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That being the case, Mr. Guy-Smith, you're still going to use this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So there's no hurry in admitting it at this point. We'll then stand adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned. Same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24
